items.source_title: Transect: Retaining Observability for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Evaluations
items.excerpt: We call the range of attributes an evaluator can reliably see or infer from an evaluation its observability envelope. --- First, within-run opacity: a final score summarises performance on a long-horizon task but obscures discarded strategies, course corrections, recoveries, unexpected behaviors, and attempts to game the evaluation. Second, a human attention bottleneck: reviewing hundreds or thousands of pages of agent activity requires scarce subject-matter expertise and the ability to connect and co-interpret complex events at distant points in a transcript. Third, insufficient statistical power: long agent evaluations are costly in time and resources, so evaluators can afford relatively few repetitions per agent and setup. Fourth, setup attribution uncertainty: observed performance is determined by both the model and the system it is embedded in.

items.excerpt: At the end of our pipeline, a single repair loop alternates deterministic checks with agent judgment and feeds any failures back to the writer agent for revision. The validation checks cover structural completeness, provenance and claim-to-source links, compilation, and venue and page budget constraints. An independent audit agent runs every round on a read-only copy of the workspace and flags where the paper's numbers, comparisons, or conclusions overclaim or contradict the canonical data and evidence trail. An optional reviewer-style agent assesses framing, caveats, figures, and clarity, and may ask the writer agent to narrow or qualify claims.
